summary.text: 用 means “use” or “put into effect.” Oracle-bone examples place it after divination statements to indicate whether a proposed action was carried out. A reported interpretation sees the graph as a container picture later borrowed for “use”; the container’s spoken name is unknown, so the proposed sound-based borrowing cannot be checked.

formation.text: The graph’s formation is disputed. One interpretation treats the whole graph as a container pictograph. The received 說文 account parses it as 卜 plus 中. Other accounts relate 用 and 同 as graphic variants or a divided graph; a separate proposal analyzes 用 as 同 with a handle added and assigns 同 a phonetic role. These accounts are unresolved, and an internal sound component is not established.

components.text: One interpretation sees the whole graph as a container, with its body on the left and handle on the right. It proposes that the graph was borrowed for “use” because the container’s name may have sounded similar, but that name is unknown and the sound match cannot be checked. Competing accounts parse or relate the graph differently.

history.text: A catalogue indexes oracle-bone, bronze, Chu manuscript, seal-script and 說文 forms, but does not describe their individual strokes or establish a detailed sequence of graphic changes.

The reported container interpretation differs from the received 說文 parsing 從卜從中. Other accounts relate 用 and 同 as graphic variants or a divided graph, or propose 同 plus a handle. These accounts are not reconciled, and 同 is not established as a phonetic component within 用.

uncertainties.text: The proposed borrowing from a container picture to “put into effect/use” cannot be checked phonetically because the depicted object’s spoken name is unknown. 用’s own reconstructed readings do not establish that name or a sound match.

Oracle-bone examples attest 用 in contexts indicating whether a proposed action was carried out, but the first occurrence and the relative chronology of this use and the proposed container sense are unsettled. A Qin-slip container or measure use read 桶 does not determine their order.

senses.text: 用/不用 is reported after divination statements to indicate whether a proposed action was carried out. This attested use does not establish the graph’s original meaning.
One Qin-slip context is read 桶, “container” or “measure.” It preserves a container-related use but does not establish the graph’s original meaning or when this use arose.

senses.gloss: preposition equivalent to 以; sequential or causal conjunction
senses.text: Bronze-inscription examples include prepositional and conjunctive uses alongside the verb “use.” The examples do not establish their relative chronology or development.
用 has the current meaning “use” or “employ.” The evidence does not establish a complete path from the attested inscriptional uses to its present range.

limitations.text: Several uses are attested, but the evidence does not establish a semantic development linking them. The proposed borrowing from a container picture to “carry out/use” lacks a verifiable sound match because the pictured object’s spoken name is unknown.

overview.text: 用 means “carry out” or “use,” as reported in oracle-bone contexts. One disputed account proposes that a container picture was reused for “use” because its name may have sounded similar; the name is unknown, so the proposed sound match cannot be checked.

components.text: One interpretation sees a handled container in the whole graph. The received 說文 parsing and separate accounts involving 同 remain unresolved.
